findings.summary: With pinned-source/ mounted but ATHENA_PIN_* unset, study jobs no longer get any validation against the tree. Nothing in the repository sets those variables, and the pinning job was dropped.
findings.evidence: The base mounted_tree() (shown with git log -L on HEAD~1) validated firstmate whenever pinned-source/ was a directory. The candidate validates only when the env pair matches a pin; otherwise it prints a WARNING. A Grep of the repository finds ATHENA_PIN_URL only in CHANGELOG.md and the rules.rs tests. The evidence snapshot shows job 20261017-205549-w45r in state 'dropped' (stale reading). Until a new pinning change lands, study verifiers do not get the tree check that the verifier prompt says code already ran. This follows the user's plan and the CHANGELOG states it, so I rated it minor, but the pinning change should be re-queued.

findings.summary: The 'not examined' placeholder check matches ordinary English in any case, so legitimate prose can trip it.
findings.evidence: placeholder_in lowercases the text before looking for 'not examined', so a real claim such as 'the retry count is not examined by the scheduler' fails the kept test. UNRESOLVED was made case-sensitive to avoid exactly this kind of false positive. A simpler fix: match an exact placeholder marker, such as the whole string or an upper-case token, the same way UNRESOLVED is matched.

findings.summary: The admission tests' planned 'fails without' filter matches only the test that admits, so Athena's revert run showed nothing about the refusals.
findings.evidence: The planned demonstration was `cargo test -p athena-cap-study admit`. It matched only a_change_inside_one_study_directory_and_the_changelog_is_admitted, which also passes on base. The refusal tests are named '..._is_refused'. I ran them directly and they pass. They would fail on base, but I know that from reading the code, not from a run.

findings.summary: When several studies of one URL exist, the ones at other SHAs fail whenever the pair names that URL.
findings.evidence: The env pair carries no study id, so two studies of one repository at different SHAs cannot both pass in a job that pins either one. The request asks for this rule, and the CHANGELOG marks it as an open question.

summary: The change does what was asked. The kept study test in rules.rs no longer hard-codes firstmate. It checks the conventions of every studies/*/ directory and runs full validation only for the study whose pin.json matches ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA. The producer prompt now states the conventions. Study admission now refuses a change that spans two studies/<id>/ directories, or one that touches anything outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md. The boundary test exempts only claim source quotes in studies/<id>/claims.json, and still scans machine-path fragments everywhere. I ran the study crate tests (40 pass; the kept test prints 'firstmate-work-handling: conventions only'), the xtask policy tests (22 pass) and the budget tests (7 pass). A Grep found none of the banned words in the changed files. Only the 7 expected files changed; nothing under studies/ and not athena.toml. The mounted case was shown only on a tree rebuilt from the study's own citations: pinned-source/ is not in this snapshot. The main caveat is a gap in the pipeline. Before this change, mounting pinned-source/ validated firstmate against it. Now that needs ATHENA_PIN_* set, and nothing in the repository sets them. The evidence snapshot shows the pinning job was dropped, so until a new pinning change lands, study jobs get conventions-only checks plus a WARNING line. The CHANGELOG says this openly, and it follows the user's own plan, so I rated it minor.
